oligos.aliases: RA36; RA-36 (TBA15 homodimer with a single dT linker, per S7 Table S1)
oligos.target_gene: F2 (thrombin / prothrombin protein; aptamer binds the thrombin PROTEIN, not F2 mRNA - no antisense mechanism)
oligos.indication: Anticoagulation (direct thrombin inhibition); short-term surgical/antithrombotic use
oligos.developer: Apto-Pharm Ltd. ('APTO-PHARM,' Ltd., Russian Federation)
oligos.max_phase: Preclinical (this source reports preclinical efficacy/PK trials in rats, marmosets and mice; no clinical phase reported)
oligos.sequence_locus: S6 Materials and Methods, 'Materials' subsection, first sentence: "DNA aptamer RA-36, dGGTTGGTGTGGTTGGTGGTTGGTGTGGTTGG⋅2 KCl, was synthesized and purified up to pharmaceutical grade for intravenous injections at ‘APTO-PHARM,’ Ltd. Russian Federation."
oligos.sugar_modifications: DNA (2'-deoxyribose; the printed "d" prefix denotes deoxyribonucleotide; source repeatedly calls it a "non-modified DNA aptamer")
oligos.conjugate: None reported; formulated as the 2 KCl salt in 0.9% NaCl at 10 mg/mL
oligos.purity_method: 'purified up to pharmaceutical grade for intravenous injections' - no numeric purity or method given
oligos.notes: Bimodular two-G-quadruplex DNA aptamer. Sequence is printed verbatim in running text (not a table/figure), so it is machine-verifiable in the XML. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by source S7 supplementary Table S1, which prints the identical 31-mer under the name 'RA36 (TBA15 homodimer)'. Molar equivalence given by S6: 7.0 mg/kg = 0.70 umole/kg (=> ~10 kDa).

measurements.system_model: Standard Human Plasma (Siemens, Germany)
measurements.delivery_method: Spiked into citrated plasma in vitro
measurements.control_description: Plasma without aptamer; Figure 1 plots "normalized values from PT test", the normalisation baseline is not given numerically
measurements.effect_vs_control: Reference species: PT prolongation by RA-36 was greater in human plasma than in any animal plasma tested.
measurements.source_locus: Figure 1 (caption + Results section "A Search for an Adequate Animal Models"); assay conditions in Methods "Assessment of Anticoagulant Activity of Aptamer RA-36 in Vitro"
measurements.verbatim_quote: Figure 1 shows that both rabbit and guinea pig blood plasma coagulation was not affected by aptamer RA-36. The coagulation of the plasma of other animals was inhibited with a somewhat lower efficiency than human plasma. measurements.timepoint: First minutes after injection (blood sampled at 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 min)
measurements.n_subjects: 10 rats per dose group (70 rats over 7 groups)
measurements.control_description: Group 1 received 0.9% sodium chloride; the saline group TT value is plotted in Figure 2A/2B but not printed numerically
measurements.effect_vs_control: Samples did not clot within 200 s, the coagulometer measurement limit - i.e. TT exceeded the upper limit of quantification for aptamer RA-36 in the first minutes after bolus.
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: the TT test turned out to be oversensitive in the first minutes for both anticoagulants
measurements.source_locus: Results, "Single Bolus Injection of Aptamer RA-36 and Bivalirudin", third sentence; censoring convention stated in the Figure 2 caption
measurements.verbatim_quote: Finally, the TT test turned out to be oversensitive in the first minutes for both anticoagulants; the samples were not clotted during 200 s, which is the measurement limit of the coagulometer.
measurements.notes: CENSORED VALUE, not a point estimate: "≥ 200" is a right-censored assay ceiling, printed as such in the Figure 2 caption ("Data points with clotting time ≥ 200 s are marked with arrows; the points corresponds non-clotting during the measurement limit of coagulometer."). It is a genuine printed number, not a value read off a plotted panel. The per-timepoint TT curves themselves are figure-only. The statement covers "both anticoagulants" - it is written once and applies to RA-36 and bivalirudin alike, so this row is duplicated per compound with the same quote. Assay: Coagulation of blood plasma was estimated with coagulometer CA-50 (Sysmex, Japan) using the reagent sets from Siemens, Germany: Test Thrombin Reagent for thrombin time (TT) determination, Thromborel® S for prothrombin time (PT) determination, Actin FS Activated PTT Reagent for activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) determination.

measurements.notes: SECONDARY/CITED VALUE: the "2 to 3-fold" figure is attributed in-line to Zavyalova et al., 2016a, not measured in this paper. Species is recorded as rat because the dose-selection narrative in this paragraph is about the rat/mouse/monkey dose ladder, but the source does not state the species for this specific 2-3 fold observation - treat species as uncertain.

measurements.system_model: Male C57Bl/6 mice, 25-31 g, 12 weeks; electrically induced carotid artery thrombosis (3 V, 200-250 mA for 60-120 s), thrombus area measured by digital video
measurements.delivery_method: Single intravenous bolus (100 uL) into the jugular vein before electrical injury
measurements.exposure_duration: Thrombus monitored 3-40 min after sample injection
measurements.control_description: Saline (0.9% NaCl) control group, same thrombosis model, same timepoint window (Table 3 row "Control")
measurements.effect_vs_control: Smaller thrombus area than the saline control at the matched timepoint; both anticoagulants reduce thrombus area dose-dependently.
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The standard deviations are rather large
measurements.source_locus: Table 3, row "Bivalirudin 0.19 mg/kg", column "The first 5 min"
measurements.notes: Values copied cell-for-cell from Table 3 (a real HTML/JATS table, not a figure). verbatim_quote is the table row with its two data cells space-joined, because JATS cell boundaries carry no printed delimiter. Table caption: "Antithrombotic efficiencies of aptamer RA-36 and bivalirudin: mean area of thrombus at the beginning and at the end of the observation.". Dosing per Methods: "A sample of 100 μl of 0.9% NaCl, or aptamer RA-36 (7, 35, and 70 mg/kg dose), or bivalirudin (0.19, 0.38, and 0.75 mg/kg dose) was bolus injected into the jugular vein.". Group sizes per Figure 6 caption: "Antithrombotic activity in the alive mice model of induced thrombosis: (A) aptamer RA-36 (7, 35, and 70 mg/kg doses; 10 animals per dose), (B) bivalirudin (0.19, 0.38, and 0.75 mg/kg doses; 6, 10, and 9 animals per dose, respectively).". Mean +/- SD as printed; n printed per group. This is a THROMBOTIC OUTCOME row (on-target antithrombotic efficacy), not a clotting-time row. The authors additionally state 0.75 mg/kg bivalirudin ~ 35 mg/kg RA-36 on this endpoint: "Two parameters were used to compare the efficiencies of aptamer RA-36 and bivalirudin: initial and final sizes of thrombus (mean areas of thrombus during the first and the last 5 min of the experiments) (Table 3). The effect of the dose of 0.75 mg/kg of bivalirudin was approximately the same with the effect of the dose of 35 mg/kg of aptamer RA-36."

measurements.notes: REGULATORY / REPORTING SILENCE (not a measured null; effect_direction is NOT_REPORTED, not "no_change"). BLEEDING WAS NEVER MEASURED. The paper motivates RA-36 by reduced bleeding risk ("This bimodular structure provides a favorable dose-effect dependence allowing the risk of bleeding to be potentially decreased") but reports no bleeding-time, blood-loss, haemoglobin or haematoma endpoint in any of the rat, marmoset or mouse experiments. This is reporting silence, not a measured null. The verbatim_quote is the Methods sentence that enumerates the complete coagulation panel the study did run, which is what makes the omission demonstrable rather than assumed.

measurements.system_model: Normal human plasma (George King Bio-Medical, KS, USA) spiked in vitro; Sysmex CA-620 automated coagulometer with Thrombocheck aPTT reagent
measurements.delivery_method: Spiked into normal plasma in vitro (pre-annealed aptamer in PBS)
measurements.exposure_duration: 1 min pre-incubation at 37 C, then 2 min with aPTT reagent, then CaCl2 recalcification
measurements.readout_unit: s (relative aPTT = sample aPTT minus control aPTT)
measurements.control_description: aptamer (−) / PBS-spiked normal human plasma; ABSOLUTE control aPTT = 27.1 s (Figure 2 caption)
measurements.effect_vs_control: Value plotted only in Figure 2B; the source states M08s-1 gave the longest relative aPTT of all monomers and drugs tested, so this compound sits below 20 s in human plasma.
measurements.source_locus: Results, "Evaluation of the anticoagulant activity of M08s-1-based bivalent aptamers by activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) in spiked plasma", monomer paragraph; panel Figure 2B; control value from the Figure 2 caption
measurements.verbatim_quote: Measurement of the drugs and monomeric aptamers at molecular equivalence (0.33 μM) in human plasma using the aPTT assay demonstrated a relative aPTT of M08s-1 at 20 s, which was the longest of those tested and was greater than that of previously reported aptamers and even of drugs (Figure 2B). This tendency was also observed in mouse plasma (Figure 2C), suggesting that M08s-1 at a monomer level was the most potent thrombin inhibitor among the tested aptamers and drugs.
measurements.notes: MATCHED-DOSE PANEL: every compound in Figure 2B/2C was tested at the same molar concentration (0.33 uM), which is what makes these rows directly comparable across compounds. Control aPTT is carried on every row per the bundle instruction. Readout is RELATIVE aPTT (a difference), defined by the source as: "The “relative aPTT” was calculated by subtracting the aPTT of PBS spiked in human plasma (27 s) from the aPTT of a tested sample spiked in human plasma.". Concentration arithmetic check: methods say 1.6 uL of 30 uM aptamer + 48.4 uL plasma + 50 uL aPTT reagent + 50 uL CaCl2 = 0.32 uM final in 150 uL, consistent with the stated 0.33 uM ("1.6 μL of each pre-annealed 30 μM aptamers in PBS and 48.4 μL of normal human plasma or normal mouse plasma were incubated at 37°C for 1 min using a fully automated blood coagulation instrument (CA-620; Sysmex, Japan). Then, 50 μL of aPTT reagent (Thrombocheck; Sysmex) was added and further incubated at 37°C for 2 min. Then, 50 μL of 0.025 M calcium chloride was added, and aPTT was measured immediately by tracking the change in scattered light intensity over time at 660 nm. The experiments were performed in triplicate."). CONTROL-VALUE CONFLICT: the body text of the same paper gives the human control as "27 s", the Figure 2 caption as 27.1 s, and supplementary Figure S12 as 28.7 s - see extraction_notes hazard #3. Compound identities for this paragraph: "We first investigated the anticoagulant activity of the monomeric M08s-1 and compared this with the known anti-thrombin DNA aptamers TBA13, TBA29, RE31,42 and NU172 (Figures S2A–S2D); in addition, the argatroban and bivalirudin anti-thrombin drugs indicative of HIT were tested (Figures S1A and S1B)." - NOTE the source writes "TBA13" here, while Figure S2a and Table S1 both give TBA15.

measurements.verbatim_quote: Measurement of the drugs and monomeric aptamers at molecular equivalence (0.33 μM) in human plasma using the aPTT assay demonstrated a relative aPTT of M08s-1 at 20 s, which was the longest of those tested and was greater than that of previously reported aptamers and even of drugs (Figure 2B). This tendency was also observed in mouse plasma (Figure 2C), suggesting that M08s-1 at a monomer level was the most potent thrombin inhibitor among the tested aptamers and drugs.

Readout is RELATIVE aPTT (a difference), defined by the source as: "The “relative aPTT” was calculated by subtracting the aPTT of PBS spiked in human plasma (27 s) from the aPTT of a tested sample spiked in human plasma.". Concentration arithmetic check: methods say 1.6 uL of 30 uM aptamer + 48.4 uL plasma + 50 uL aPTT reagent + 50 uL CaCl2 = 0.32 uM final in 150 uL, consistent with the stated 0.33 uM ("1.6 μL of each pre-annealed 30 μM aptamers in PBS and 48.4 μL of normal human plasma or normal mouse plasma were incubated at 37°C for 1 min using a fully automated blood coagulation instrument (CA-620; Sysmex, Japan). Then, 50 μL of aPTT reagent (Thrombocheck; Sysmex) was added and further incubated at 37°C for 2 min. Then, 50 μL of 0.025 M calcium chloride was added, and aPTT was measured immediately by tracking the change in scattered light intensity over time at 660 nm. The experiments were performed in triplicate."). measurements.verbatim_quote: The aPTT assay in human plasma showed that the two heterodimers, Lin08-29 and Pse08-29, exhibited a similar degree of prolongation of the relative aPTT than the previously reported heterodimer 0/0A2/0A4 (relative aPTT = 49 s). measurements.notes: MATCHED-DOSE PANEL: every compound in Figure 2B/2C was tested at the same molar concentration (0.33 uM), which is what makes these rows directly comparable across compounds. Control aPTT is carried on every row per the bundle instruction. Readout is RELATIVE aPTT (a difference), defined by the source as: "The “relative aPTT” was calculated by subtracting the aPTT of PBS spiked in human plasma (27 s) from the aPTT of a tested sample spiked in human plasma.". Concentration arithmetic check: methods say 1.6 uL of 30 uM aptamer + 48.4 uL plasma + 50 uL aPTT reagent + 50 uL CaCl2 = 0.32 uM final in 150 uL, consistent with the stated 0.33 uM ("1.6 μL of each pre-annealed 30 μM aptamers in PBS and 48.4 μL of normal human plasma or normal mouse plasma were incubated at 37°C for 1 min using a fully automated blood coagulation instrument (CA-620; Sysmex, Japan). measurements.verbatim_quote: Although argatroban required approximately 12 μM to reach the maximum therapeutic window of 50 s of relative aPTT, M08s-1 could reach the time at a 3-fold lower concentration (4 μM). Furthermore, four M08s-1-based bivalent aptamers nearly reached 50 s of relative aPTT at 0.3–0.45 μM, suggesting that these aptamers were effective at 30-fold and 10-fold lower concentrations compared with argatroban and monomeric M08s-1, respectively.
measurements.notes: POTENCY ROW READ THE OTHER WAY ROUND: the printed number is the CONCENTRATION required to hit a fixed 50 s relative-aPTT threshold, so dose_value carries the concentration and readout_value carries the fixed 50 s endpoint. The full concentration-response curves are in Figure 2D and are NOT extracted. The 50 s threshold is derived by the authors from the unfractionated-heparin therapeutic window (2- to 3-fold over a 27 s naive aPTT => 27-54 s relative aPTT). The 0.3-0.45 uM figure is given for the four bivalent aptamers collectively, not per compound - do not treat 0.3-0.45 as a per-compound EC.

measurements.verbatim_quote: Next, mice were dosed with monomeric aptamers and argatroban at 0.13 μmol/kg dose and four M08s-1-dimeric aptamers at 0.04 μmol/kg, and blood was collected until 1 h after administration. Despite their lower injection doses than the monomers and argatroban, all dimeric aptamers showed high anticoagulant activity based on the aPTT (Figure 3C).
measurements.notes: NO NUMBER EXTRACTED - Figure 3C is a time-course plot. Dose arithmetic check from Methods: 50 uL of 16 uM = 0.8 nmol in a 22 g mouse = 0.036 umol/kg, consistent with the stated 0.04 umol/kg. NOTE: the Discussion of the same paper writes this dose as "0.04 mg/kg" ("ically unmodified and showed sufficient efficacy at the lower dose of 0.04 mg/kg, suggesting less risk for nonspecific prolongation of aPTT.") - that is a unit error in the source; umol/kg is correct. Figure 3C caption also says "collected serum" while the Methods collect citrated PLASMA.

measurements.verbatim_quote: Among the aptamers, M08s-based Lin08-08 and Pse08-29 prolonged the PT slightly longer than others, which is the same trend as with aPTT. In all cases, the effects of aPPT were significant compared with PT, which was the same trend as for DTIs seen with the therapeutic dose.
measurements.notes: NO NUMBER EXTRACTED - PT values are plotted only in supplementary Figure S8. Dose and control taken from the Figure S8 legend: "The dose of injected samples was aligned to 0.13 µmol/kg for all compounds." and "Relative PT was gained by subtracting the treated data by 11.7 sec, an averaged value of aptamer (–) as control PT in a triplicate.". Only Lin08-08 and Pse08-29 are named individually in the text; the other rows rest on the legend statement that the PT assay was run on the same injected samples at a dose aligned to 0.13 umol/kg for all compounds. The PT/aPTT dissociation is the toxicologically interesting part: these aptamers move the intrinsic pathway far more than the extrinsic one.

measurements.source_locus: Results, paragraph beginning "Besides aPTT, prothrombin time (PT) is also measured for approved direct thrombin inhibitors"; supplementary Figures S8a/S8b (mmc1.pdf p.10)
measurements.verbatim_quote: Among the aptamers, M08s-based Lin08-08 and Pse08-29 prolonged the PT slightly longer than others, which is the same trend as with aPTT. measurements.notes: NO NUMBER EXTRACTED - PT values are plotted only in supplementary Figure S8. measurements.system_model: Purified human alpha-thrombin (6.25 nM) plus purified human fibrinogen (6 uM); turbidity at 350 nm read on an Epoch plate reader
measurements.delivery_method: Aptamer (12.5 nM) pre-incubated with thrombin 15 min at room temperature, then fibrinogen added
measurements.control_description: No-aptamer thrombin + fibrinogen clotting curve; the control clotting time is plotted in Figure 1D/1E but never printed numerically
measurements.effect_vs_control: Grouped by the source's own Figure S3b annotation under "No inhibition" (X = 0, 9, 13, or 21 bp).
measurements.source_locus: Results, "Design of M08s-1-based bivalent anti-thrombin aptamers" (Figures 1D and 1E); "No inhibition" grouping from supplementary Figure S3b (mmc1.pdf p.4)
measurements.verbatim_quote: When the duplex linker was composed of base pairs with homo-dT and homo-dA chains, where the base pair length was variable (X = 0, 5, 9, 13, 17, and 21 bp in Figure 1C), the clotting was nearly completely inhibited by a linker length with 5 and 17 bp, reflecting high anticoagulant activity via thrombin inhibition (Figure 1D).
measurements.notes: THROMBIN CLOTTING TIME (TCT) in a PURIFIED fibrinogen system, not plasma - assay defined by the source as: "Screening of the duplex linker was performed based on thrombin clotting time (TCT) with purified fibrinogen, where fibrin cleaved from fibrinogen by thrombin spontaneously aggregates to increase the turbidity of the solution as a result of “clotting”; inhibition of thrombin by the aptamer prolongs the clotting time (Figure 1C)." and run per "Briefly, to a 0.6-mL tube, 100 μL of pre-annealed 12.5 nM aptamer in PBS and 100 μL of 6.25 nM human thrombin in PBS were added and incubated at room temperature for 15 min.". NO NUMBER EXTRACTED: every clotting time in this screen is plotted only in Figure 1D/1E. effect_direction "no_change" for this variant rests on the source's OWN Figure S3b annotation, which prints "X = 5 or 17 bp X = 0, 9, 13, or 21 bp No inhibition"; the body text only says 5 and 17 bp were the active lengths. A reviewer should treat this as the source asserting a null, not as a quantified null. Figure S3 legend: "(b) Possible mechanism for strong inhibition activity of the Pse08- 29 with 5 bp and 17 bp linkers. These would be either 2:2 or 3:3 complex forms and when an inappropriate, rigid linker doesn’t allow two aptamer moieties to simultaneously bind to the same a- Thrombin.". This series is the clean sequence-to-phenotype block of the bundle: 11 near-identical constructs differing only in duplex-linker length and composition, each with a published sequence, showing a non-monotonic 5 bp / 17 bp activity window.

extraction_notes:
=== WHAT IS IN THIS BUNDLE ===
Two open-access anti-thrombin aptamer papers. S6 (RA-36) is the sequence-to-phenotype anchor: a published sequence in
running text tied to in vivo TT/PT/APTT across rat, marmoset and mouse plus a mg/kg potency equivalence against
bivalirudin. S7 (M08s-1 dimers) is the density anchor: 14 named compounds measured at one matched molar concentration
(0.33 uM) with stated absolute control clotting times, plus a full published sequence table.

=== HAZARD 1: ALMOST EVERY CLOTTING NUMBER IN THESE TWO PAPERS IS IN A FIGURE, NOT A TABLE ===
Neither paper prints a table of clotting times. S6 Figures 2, 3 and 5 (TT/PT/APTT vs time, rats and marmosets) and
S7 Figures 1D, 1E, 2B, 2C, 2D, 3B, 3C, 4B, 4C, S8 and S12 are all plots. No value was read off any of them.
Where the endpoint exists only in a panel, readout_value is NOT_REPORTED and readout_is_qualitative is true, and the
row says so. The numeric clotting values that DO exist are only these, all printed as text:
  S6: TT >= 200 s (censored assay ceiling, rats, both compounds); "2 to 3-fold" PT/APTT at 7.0 mg/kg (cited to prior work).
  S7: relative aPTT 20 s (M08s-1, human), 49 s (0/0A2/0A4, human), 70 s (Lin08-08, human), 85 s (Pse08-08, human),
      40 s (Lin08-29, mouse), 50 s (Pse08-29, mouse), 43 -> 19 s (Pse08-29 with the selected antidote, human);
      concentrations to reach a 50 s relative aPTT: ~12 uM argatroban, 4 uM M08s-1, 0.3-0.45 uM for the four dimers;
      controls 27.1 s (human), 25.1 s (mouse), 22.6 s (mouse in vivo aPTT), 11.7 s (mouse in vivo PT), 28.7 s (Fig S12).
S6's Table 3 (thrombus area, mm2) is a genuine table and is transcribed cell-for-cell.

=== HAZARD 2: S7 DOSE CONTRADICTION (0.13 vs 1.3 umol/kg) ===
S7 body text and Methods both say the in vivo molar-equivalent dose was 0.13 umol/kg. The Figure 3B caption says
"a uniform dose of 1.3 μmol/kg" - a 10-fold discrepancy. 0.13 umol/kg is used throughout this extraction because
(a) the body states it twice, (b) supplementary Figure S8 repeats 0.13 umol/kg, and (c) the Methods arithmetic gives it:
50 uL of 52 uM = 2.6 nmol into a 22 g mouse = 0.118 umol/kg. The Figure 3B caption is judged a source typo.
Related unit slip in the same paper: the Discussion writes the low dose as "0.04 mg/kg" where every other mention
(body, Methods, Figure 3C) says 0.04 umol/kg.

=== HAZARD 3: S7 HAS THREE DIFFERENT HUMAN-PLASMA CONTROL aPTT VALUES ===
27 s (body text, definition of relative aPTT), 27.1 s (Figure 2 caption), 28.7 s (supplementary Figure S12 legend).
The Figure 2 series uses Thrombocheck aPTT reagent and the Figure S12/Figure 4 neutralisation series uses Actin FSL,
which plausibly explains the 27.1 vs 28.7 difference, but the paper never reconciles them. Each row here carries the
control value belonging to ITS OWN experiment, and says which. Do not pool 27.1-based and 28.7-based relative aPTTs.

=== HAZARD 4: S7 NAMING SLIPS ===
(a) The Results sentence listing the monomer comparators writes "TBA13"; Figure S2a and supplementary Table S1 both
    name it TBA15 and print a 15-mer (GGTTGGTGTGGTTGG). Treated as TBA15.
(b) The body writes "TBA15-dA15-TBA29" while Table S1 writes "TBA15-A15-TBA29" - same molecule.
(c) Figure S12 is titled "Screening of antidotes against Pese08-29" (typo for Pse08-29).
(d) The neutralisation Results sentence says the antidote screen was done "in human serum"; the Methods and the
    Figure S12 legend both say normal human PLASMA. Plasma is recorded.
(e) Figure 3C caption says "collected serum"; the Methods collect citrated plasma.
(f) The Figure 4C caption gives protamine and aptamer concentrations in mg/mL; the Methods give the identical numbers
    in ug/mL. ug/mL is the internally consistent reading (0.333 uM of a 106-mer ~ 5.6 ug/mL).
(g) Antidote concentration is 5.33 uM in the Figure S12 legend and 5.28 uM (= 16 x 0.33) in the Figure 4B legend.
(h) Figure S12 shows NINE antidote strands (including [Lin-M08s full]c) but supplementary Table S1 lists only EIGHT.
    Only the eight that appear in Table S1 are recorded as oligos; the ninth is noted here rather than transcribed.

=== HAZARD 5: S6 INTERNAL ROUNDING SLIP ===
The Results give the bivalirudin therapeutic dose as "0.75 mg/kg = 0.34 umole/kg"; the Discussion equivalence sentence
says "0.35 umole/kg dose of bivalirudin". Same dose, inconsistent rounding.

=== HOW THE S7 SEQUENCES WERE OBTAINED, AND WHY THEY ARE TRUSTWORTHY ===
S7 puts every sequence in supplementary Table S1, and Table S1 is embedded in mmc1.pdf (page 14) as a single raster
image with NO text layer - PyMuPDF returns only the caption. The supplement is also not reachable through PMC or
Europe PMC (see the S7 retrieval_route field). The sequences were therefore obtained by rendering page 14 at 420-700
dpi and reading the table visually. Because visual transcription is exactly the kind of step this project treats as a
fabrication risk, every sequence was then validated four independent ways before being written here:
  (1) LENGTH: the transcribed length equals the "Length (mer)" printed in the same table row - all 23 rows pass.
  (2) REVERSE-COMPLEMENT CLOSURE: for all 11 pseudo-circular constructs, revcomp(internal linker) equals
      3'-overhang + 5'-overhang exactly. A single misread base anywhere in a linker or overhang breaks this.
  (3) INDEPENDENT MACHINE TEXT: Figure S3a and Figure S12a in the SAME PDF do have extractable text, and they
      reproduce the 17-bp and 21-bp linker duplexes and the M08s-1 segment and its complements character-for-character.
      revcomp(M08s-1 as transcribed) equals [M08s-1 full]c as transcribed, and equals the reversed 3'->5' string that
      PDF text extraction recovers from Figure S12.
  (4) CROSS-SOURCE: Table S1's "RA36" is character-identical to the RA-36 sequence printed in the running text of S6
      (GGTTGGTGTGGTTGGTGGTTGGTGTGGTTGG), which is machine-extractable from the S6 XML.
Nevertheless: sequence_locus on every S7 oligo states that Table S1 is a raster image. A reviewer who needs
regulatory-grade sequence provenance should re-verify against the publisher PDF.
S6's RA-36 sequence needs none of this - it is printed in running text and is machine-verifiable in the XML.

=== WHY "modifications" IS EMPTY ===
Both papers use unmodified DNA. S6 calls RA-36 a "non-modified DNA aptamer" and prints it with the "d" prefix;
S7 states "the M08s-1-based bivalent aptamers were chemically unmodified" and heads Table S1 "ssDNA Sequence (5' to 3')".
But neither publishes PER-POSITION chemistry - there is no case convention, no legend, no position-indexed modification
table. Per the contract, a uniform global statement is not per-position chemistry, so nothing was modelled: the
information is carried at the oligo level in backbone_chemistry / sugar_modifications / ps_count instead. Note that
backbone_chemistry is set to full_PO only for the compounds the source explicitly calls chemically unmodified
(RA-36, M08s-1 and its four dimers); for TBA15, TBA29, NU172, RE-31, RA36-as-listed-in-S7, the 0/0A2/0A4 strands,
the antidotes and the linker-optimisation series it is left NOT_REPORTED, because "ssDNA" in a table header is a
weaker claim than an explicit statement about backbone chemistry.

=== NON-OLIGONUCLEOTIDE RECORDS THAT MUST BE FILTERED OUT DOWNSTREAM ===
Three records in "oligos" are NOT oligonucleotides and are present only because they are the matched, same-experiment
comparators that make the aptamer potency anchors interpretable:
  OLG_BIVALIRUDIN  - 20-residue peptide (MW 2180.32), the reference drug in S6 and a comparator in S7.
  OLG_ARGATROBAN   - small molecule (MW 508.64), the approved HIT drug and the matched comparator in S7.
  OLG_PEGAPTANIB   - a real aptamer, but S7 does not measure it; its single row is a cited third-party claim.
Each is flagged in its own notes field. Any oligonucleotide-only analysis must exclude the first two.

=== PLATELET / THROMBOCYTOPENIA BOUNDARY ===
S7's indication is heparin-induced THROMBOCYTOPENIA, but the paper measures no platelet parameter whatsoever - PF4 and
HIT immunology appear only as Introduction background. No platelet_coag_crosstalk row with data was created. Two
explicit reporting-silence rows record the absence, so that a curator merging this bundle with the thrombocytopenia
dossier can see that these sources contribute nothing there.

=== ON-TARGET vs UNINTENDED ===
Every row except the pegaptanib row is ON-TARGET pharmacology: these are anticoagulants and the clotting-time
prolongation is the intended effect. on_target_effect=false is used only for the scrambled-sequence negative control
(OLG_M08S1_SCM), the absence rows, and the pegaptanib row - which is the only unintended_toxicity=true row in the bundle.
That imbalance is a real property of this bundle and should not be read as absence of oligonucleotide coagulation
toxicity in general.

=== ADJACENT SOURCE NOT EXTRACTED ===
/home/user/coag-staging/fulltext/PMC12677840.xml is on disk and is the direct follow-up to S7 (Stick08-29 sticky-end
split-strand series, same aPTT assay, control 27.8 s, and it states Pse08-29 is 106 nt - which independently confirms
this bundle's Pse08-29 length). It was NOT extracted because it is not one of this bundle's two assigned sources. Its
own sequences are likewise in a supplementary Table S1. It is a strong candidate for a follow-on bundle.
refused_rows:
Things that looked extractable and were deliberately NOT written as rows:

1. EVERY CLOTTING TIME THAT EXISTS ONLY IN A PLOTTED PANEL. This is by far the largest refusal: S6 Figures 2, 3 and 5
   (three assays x two compounds x three doses x seven timepoints x two species - on the order of 250 plotted values)
   and S7 Figures 2B, 2C, 2D, 3B, 3C, 4B, 4C, S8a, S8b, S12b (another ~150). Reading a bar height or a curve point
   would have multiplied the row count several-fold. Refused outright; the corresponding rows carry NOT_REPORTED with
   readout_is_qualitative true and name the panel.

2. SPR BINDING CONSTANTS (S7 Table 1 and Figure S5): KD values for M08s, TBA29, Lin08-08, Pse08-08 and Pse08-29
   against human and mouse thrombin (47.2 / 36.9 / 0.4 / 0.4 / 2.6 nM human; 495 / 22.0 / 6.7 / 4.2 / 6.3 nM mouse),
   plus ka and kd. These are real, numeric, in a real table, and highly relevant to the compounds - but they are
   TARGET-BINDING affinities, not coagulation readouts. Forcing them into readout_category "anticoagulant_activity"
   would let a downstream model treat a KD as a clotting phenotype. Left out on purpose; a binding-affinity table is
   the right home for them. (The one apparent exception in this file, the S6 Ki row, is admitted because the source
   frames it as thrombin INHIBITION potency and it is explicitly labelled as a secondary/cited value.)

3. SERUM/NUCLEASE STABILITY (S7 Figure S11c: half-lives 6.9 / >8.0 / >8.0 / 7.8 / >8.0 / >8.0 h in human serum and
   2.4 / 3.8 / 4.0 / 3.3 / 0.6 / 0.7 h in mouse serum) and PHARMACOKINETICS (S7 Figure 3E half-lives; S6 Tables 1 and 2
   AUC, MRT, Vss, clearance, kel, two-compartment parameters). Numeric and tabulated, but ADME, not coagulopathy.
   Refused as out-of-endpoint. Noted here because a PK/ADME bundle would want them and they are cheap to lift.

4. S7 AVIDITY RATIOS (Figure S6b: 0.762 / 0.728 / 0.822 / 0.785 / 0.553 / 0.529 / 0.549 / 0.642). The values survive
   PDF text extraction, but the legend does not label which number belongs to which aptamer/species pair unambiguously
   once the panel layout is lost. Assigning them would have required guessing the plot order. Refused.

5. THE NINTH S7 ANTIDOTE, [Lin-M08s full]c. Figure S12 shows nine antidote strands; supplementary Table S1 prints
   only eight. Its sequence is recoverable by reversing the 3'->5' string that PDF text extraction pulls from Figure
   S12, and the reversal is consistent with the naming pattern ([M08s-1 full]c + CTAGTGAC = 51 nt) - but it is absent
   from the authoritative sequence table, so it was not written as an oligo. Flagged in extraction_notes instead.

6. THE S6 SUPPLEMENTARY THROMBUS DATASET. S6 states "all the data are listed in the Supplementary Material" for the
   per-animal thrombus areas. That file was not retrieved, so no per-animal rows were written - only the Table 3 means.

7. GUINEA-PIG SPECIES MAPPING. The contract's species enum has no guinea pig. Rather than mis-map it to "rat" or
   "rabbit" or blank it to NOT_APPLICABLE, the row carries species "guinea_pig" (out-of-enum but truthful) and the
   deviation is flagged. Same reasoning for recording Macaca mulatta and Callithrix jacchus as species "monkey" with
   the actual species in system_model - the two are pharmacologically different here and should not be silently merged.

8. PLATELET COUNTS. Neither source measures one, so no platelet row with data exists to refuse - but note explicitly

9. IN VIVO EFFICACY / BLEEDING FOR S7's COMPOUNDS. None exists; the authors say so. Recorded as an absence row rather
   than silently omitted, and NOT recorded as a measured null.

10. FIGURE 1D/1E PER-VARIANT TCT VALUES. The linker-length series rows carry a direction but no number. For the
    inactive lengths (0, 9, 13, 21 bp) even the DIRECTION rests on the source's own Figure S3b annotation
